jobs.title: Summer Safety Associate (Summer 2027) at Clark Construction Group
jobs.description: Employer: Clark Construction Group Expires: 10/05/2026 The Summer Associate – Safety role provides you with the unique opportunity to safeguard the health and well-being of thousands of craft workers and team members across our jobsites. Working directly alongside Clark’s safety and operational leaders, you will gain hands-on field experience advancing company safety policies, programs, and procedures while actively driving our 24/7 "Culture of Care.” We empower you to take on significant responsibility early, backing your growth with extensive resources, mentorship, formal training, and a culture that challenges you to advance your career further. Here, the standard is higher. Our team doesn't just build landmark projects—we build the leaders who make them possible. The Role The Summer Associate Program is your opportunity to build a comprehensive understanding of the construction industry and our business. As a summer associate, you will be fully embedded with a team on a jobsite or in a department, gaining hands-on experience. Beyond your project work, you will become an integrated member of the Clark community through training and development opportunities. Build your network through social events and jobsite tours, and sharpen your skills with formal training sessions led by Clark experts. Other cornerstones of the Summer Associate Program include: The Capstone Project: A team-based project that challenges you to develop innovative solutions for real-time business opportunities. You will present your findings directly to company leadership, gaining visibility and the chance to make a tangible impact. The Passport Experience: A curated series of experiences designed to guide your summer journey. The Passport showcases the full breadth of Clark’s business, helps you establish meaningful connections across the company, and ensures you gain essential industry knowledge. This immersive, full-time program runs for 8 -10 weeks and begins in late May or early June. Responsibilities Throughout the summer, you will be exposed to: Program Implementation: Assisting in executing corporate and project-specific safety and health programs in alignment with federal, state, and local safety standards.Culture & Education: Helping promote a proactive safety culture by coaching, mentoring, and educating trade partners and internal team members on occupational health and safety requirements.Field Inspections & Analytics: Conducting daily jobsite walks to monitor safety compliance, track metrics, and assist in reporting project safety performance and forward-looking plans.Safety Planning: Partnering closely with field superintendents and project leadership to plan for high-risk operations, including critical crane lifts, hazardous material handling, fire prevention, and site evacuation strategies. Basic QualificationsCurrently attending university and working to complete a bachelor's degree in Occupational Health and SafetyInterest and passion for the construction industry The work environment and requirements described below are representative of those necessary for an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this role. The Physical Side of the Role: This is an active, hands-on role. You can expect to be on your feet frequently, navigating active job sites with uneven terrain, stairs, ladders, and hoists. The work is physically demanding and requires a full range of motion, including bending, kneeling, and reaching. You’ll need to be comfortable frequently lifting and carrying materials up to 25 pounds, and occasionally up to 50 pounds. This role requires the ability to communicate effectively, as well as visual acuity for reading plans and inspecting work. The role does include desk time in the office that may require prolonged periods of sitting for tasks like computer work, document review, and meetings. Your Work Environment: You’ll spend a significant amount of your time on active construction sites, which means being adaptable to all kinds of weather and moderate to loud noise levels, and comfortable in elevated or confined work areas with moving mechanical equipment and with the fast-paced nature of a project in progress. You will also spend time in a typical office setting with moderate noise levels. Your safety is our top priority, and you'll be expected to follow Clark Construction's safety policies and procedures, and all applicable laws, at all locations. Our High-Performing Culture: This is a demanding, high-performance environment. We are looking for candidates who are energized by challenge, thrive under pressure, and are prepared to do what it takes to achieve exceptional results. Success in this role requires significant commitment, including flexibility to work extended hours, especially during critical project phases or client deadlines. A Drug Free Workplace: Clark promotes a drug free workplace. A pre-employment fitness for duty screening is required, and random fitness for duty tests of employees are conducted quarterly. Clark offers a total compensation package. Benefits could include commuter benefits or fitness reimbursement. Hourly rates will be determined by factors such as geographic location, education, experience, and market considerations. For this role the hourly rate is $23 - $29/ hr.

jobs.description: Employer: SRC, Inc Expires: 10/05/2026 SRC, Inc. is currently seeking summer 2027 Machine Learning Engineering interns for our Dayton, OH or Syracuse, NY locations who enjoy solving interesting problems using ML. Are you excited about machine learning (ML) and want to do something meaningful? Do you want your work to make a real difference and save lives? Our products protect our soldiers, our nation, and our allies. We solve the kinds of problems search engines don't have answers for. Selected candidates will have the opportunity to work in small teams designing and developing solutions using deep learning and statistical methods on a variety of challenging problems. Because of the diverse nature of our work, we can accommodate team members with varying technical backgrounds. jobs.title: Technology Undergraduate Summer Internship at Wellington Management Company LLP
jobs.description: Employer: Wellington Management Company LLP Expires: 10/06/2026 WELLINGTON MANAGEMENTWellington Management offers comprehensive investment management capabilities that span nearly all segments of the global capital markets. Our investment solutions, tailored to the unique return and risk objectives of institutional clients in more than 50 countries, draw on a robust body of proprietary research and a collaborative culture that encourages independent thought and healthy debate. As a private partnership, we believe our ownership structure fosters a long-term view that aligns our perspectives with those of our clients.Wellington Management is seeking motivated undergraduate students to join our 2027 Technology Summer Internship Program. This 10-week paid internship provides hands-on software engineering experience, mentorship, and exposure to the investment management industry and the technologies that support it. Technology plays a critical role in enabling Wellington's investment, business, and client teams. Our technologist's partner with teams across the firm to build innovative solutions, improve decision-making, and support the needs of a global investment organization. Interns will work full-time (40 hours/week) at our Boston headquarters beginning June 2027. Interns are eligible for a housing stipend and a flexible work model that includes four days per week in the office and one remote workday. Designed for students from a variety of academic backgrounds, this program is intended for candidates with prior experience in software engineering, data analysis, computer science, information systems, or a related technical field who want to apply those skills to building practical technology solutions. Interns will have the opportunity to explore career paths in Wellington’s technology organization and do meaningful work alongside experienced professionals. What You'll DoAs a summer intern, you will work alongside a cohort of fellow interns on a summer-long project focused on building a software solution that addresses a real business challenge at Wellington. Working as part of a project team, you'll gain hands-on experience in software engineering, data analysis, and product-oriented problem solving while developing technical, professional, and leadership skills. Summer Project ExperienceCollaborate with fellow interns to identify, design, build, test and deliver a software application that addresses a real business challenge facing Wellington.Analyze user needs, gather feedback, and apply creative problem-solving to develop solutions that drive meaningful business impact.Gain hands-on experience applying software engineering and data analysis skills, including requirements gathering, application design, coding, testing, user feedback, and iterative delivery.Take ownership of a key project workstream while partnering closely with teammates and stakeholders to achieve shared goals.Build relationships across the firm through networking, collaboration, and engagement with business and technology professionals.Present project outcomes, recommendations, and lessons learned to senior leaders at the conclusion of the program.Work on challenges that evolve each year to reflect changing business priorities, emerging technologies, and opportunities for innovation. What You'll GainThroughout the program, interns will:Gain exposure to the intersection of technology, business, and investment management within a global asset management firm.Experience how diverse technology disciplines work together to solve complex business challenges and deliver value for clients and colleagues.Develop technical, analytical, and professional skills through hands-on experience, mentorship and real-world project work.Build meaningful relationships with leaders, professionals, and fellow interns across the firm.Strengthen communication, collaboration, leadership, and problem-solving skills in a supportive and team-oriented way.Gain confidence presenting ideas, influencing stakeholders and translating complex concepts into actionable recommendations.Explore potential career paths within technology while developing a deeper understanding of Wellington’s culture and business. Who Should Apply We welcome students from a broad range of majors, backgrounds, experiences, and academic disciplines. Candidates should have experience applying technical skills through coursework, internships, research, independent projects, or other hands-on work in software engineering, data analysis, computer science, information systems, or a related field. We look for:Current sophomore or junior undergraduate students pursuing a bachelor's degree.Strong communication, organizational, and problem-solving skills.Experience with software engineering, data analysis, or a related technical field, including familiarity with at least one programming language such as Python.Involvement in campus organizations, leadership activities, volunteer work, or other extracurricular experiences.Ability to work effectively in a collaborative team environment.No prior finance experience is required.Curious and adaptable in exploring emerging technologies and AI tools in your work, school, and projects This position is not eligible for visa sponsorship.Application Deadline: October 2, 2026 JOB TITLETechnology Undergraduate Summer Internship LOCATION280 Congress Not sure you meet 100% of our qualifications? That’s ok. If you believe that you could excel in this role, we encourage you to apply and welcome a chance to review your background. We are dedicated to building and maintaining a diversified workforce and considering a broad array of candidates with a variety of skill, workplace experiences, and backgrounds. As an equal opportunity employer, Wellington Management considers all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, religion, creed, national origin, age, ancestry, disability (physical or mental), medical condition, citizenship, marital status, pregnancy, veteran or military status, genetic information or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. If you are a candidate with a disability, or are assisting a candidate with a disability, and require an accommodation to apply for one of our jobs, please email us at GMWTalentOperations@wellington.com At Wellington Management, our approach to compensation is designed to help us attract, inspire and retain the best talent in our industry. We strive to pay employees fairly and competitively across all levels and roles. Our approach to compensation considers all aspects of total compensation; all employees are eligible to receive salary, variable compensation, and benefits. The base salary range for this position is: $19-$35 per hourThis range takes into account the wide range of factors that are considered when making compensation decisions, including but not limited to skill sets; role; skills and experience; certifications; and education. This range is an estimate, and further details on salary and total compensation aspects will be shared with candidates during the recruitment process. Base salary is only one component of Wellington’s total compensation approach. Other rewards may include a discretionary Corporate Bonus and/ or Incentives, if eligible. In addition, we offer a comprehensive and high value benefit package to meet the unique needs of our employees and their families, and we are committed to fostering a flexible work environment that enables employees to thrive personally and professionally. Examples of our benefits include retirement plan, health and wellbeing, dental, vision, and pharmacy coverage, health savings account, flexible spending accounts and commuter program, employee assistance program, life and disability insurance, adoption assistance, back-up childcare, tuition/CFA reimbursement and paid time off (leave of absence, paid holidays, volunteer, sick and vacation time). flows, logging, backups and relevant third-party services.• Helping to create and validate inventories of key IT and OT-related assets, software, data and suppliers.• Reviewing existing cybersecurity controls and identifying potential risks, vulnerabilities and areas for improvement.• Supporting a baseline gap assessment against appropriate cybersecurity good practice and relevant frameworks such as ISO/IEC 27001, IEC 62443 and Cyber Essentials.• Reviewing areas such as user access, MFA, privileged accounts, device security, patching, backups, encryption, remote access, logging and incident response.• Researching appropriate technical solutions and good practice where potential improvements are identified.• Helping to document existing controls, processes and technical arrangements in a clear and structured way.• Supporting the cybersecurity review of ECS's patent-pending remote OT connection technology, helping to assess its architecture, access controls, data flows, remote connectivity and security controls against recognised cybersecurity good practice.• Working with ECS engineers, developers and management to understand how cybersecurity requirements need to work alongside practical engineering and customer requirements.• Producing a final summary of findings and contributing to a prioritised cybersecurity improvement roadmap, identifying recommended actions, priorities and potential next steps for ECS.By the end of the 12-week internship, the successful candidate will have contributed to a documented cybersecurity baseline and prioritised improvement roadmap for ECS, including recommendations to support the continued secure development of our Connect remote OT technology and Command Centre platform.Who Should ApplyWe are looking for someone who:• work with people from different technical backgrounds.• Is curious, practical and keen to learn, with an ability to look beyond theory and consider how cybersecurity controls can be implemented effectively within a real business environment.Candidates must be able to start immediatelyCandidates must accept or decline an internship within 5 working days of an offer being madePlease make us jobs.description: Employer: Beyond New Horizons Expires: 10/09/2026 Job Title: Aerospace, Mechanical Engineering Internship 2027 – Tunnel 9 Location: Maryland: AEDC White Oak Campus MDJob Family Code: O - EngineeringFunction/Branch: Tunnel 9Directorate: Test OperationsPosition Type: Full Time / SeasonalPay Type: Non-ExemptSponsorship: Position Not SponsoredGrade: M04 (OB0404) – M05 (OB0503)Salary Range or Starting Hourly Rate: $31.23 -$40.83/ per hour OverviewOpen to External candidates. Beyond New Horizons, LLC (BNH) has an exciting opportunity for seasonal Aerospace, Electrical, and Mechanical Engineering Interns, supporting TOS II, at Tunnel 9 in Silver Spring, MD. Job SummaryTunnel 9 is a geographically separated unit of Arnold Engineering Development Complex (AEDC). It provides aerodynamic simulation capabilities critical to hypersonic-system and vehicle-technology development at speeds from Mach 7 to Mach 18.The BNH Internship Program offers full-time summer internship opportunities lasting 10 to 12 weeks for undergraduate and graduate engineering students. Interns are paired with experienced engineers and scientists who mentor them while they complete assigned projects, gain practical experience in their field of study, and contribute to the Air Force and BNH missions. Interns will brief senior management summarizing work accomplished, lessons learned and recommended next actions. Job Duties:The Tunnel 9 internship provides interns with multiple projects throughout the summer, exposing them to the range of engineering work performed at AEDC Tunnel 9. Assignments address practical engineering challenges that support Air Force and BNH missions. Examples of previous and planned intern assignments include the following; this list is illustrative and not exhaustive:Operate and conduct tests in Tunnel 9’s research and development (R&D) Mach 3 tunnel and install test article hardware and instrumentation in support of active customer testing at Mach 7–18.Validate test article data-acquisition system configurations and nomenclature; conduct pre-test instrumentation integrity checks; and perform model hardware changes between test runs.Support the development and application of temperature-sensitive paint, infrared thermography, fast-response piezoelectric force-balance instrumentation, balance-calibration software, and test article boundary-layer transition measurements and analysis.Develop graphical user interfaces to process, analyze, and decode test article and tunnel-facility data; develop or modify hardware and software interfaces for integrated data-acquisition and processing systems; and repair malfunctioning test article instrumentation.Create and modify electrical schematics using AutoCAD; research power load-bank systems for potential use with emergency generator systems; and assist with the field implementation, validation, and verification of new or modified measurement, data-acquisition, and control systems.Improve or add limit indicators to network and facility human-machine interface (HMI) screens; analyze optical measurement systems and recommend upgrades from analog drive motors to stepper-motor technology; and develop or modify programmable logic controller (PLC) ladder logic and HMI screens for facility control systems.Configure and program digital servo amplifiers and other facility control-system hardware; develop improved system-controller interfaces; and perform system integration, checkout, troubleshooting, drawing redlines, and work-instruction improvements for test cell systems.Research and prepare technical documentation and recommendations for operationally feasible dew-point measurement hardware; develop portable electronic devices for timing and calibrating high-speed camera systems; and build servo-valve models in MATLAB Simulink.Create three-dimensional models of subsystem components in PTC Creo; design and 3D-print fixtures for alignment, installation, and gauge inspections; design large hardware carts for assembly work; and improve and document 3D-printing methods to increase print accuracy.Refine heat-transfer code for improved integration with ANSYS and Creo; conduct material, structural, and thermo-structural analyses using ANSYS; and design hardware to support test cell and test article customer-testing activities.Update statistical probability-of-failure analyses for high-pressure vessels rated from 20,000 to 60,000 psi; and perform field verification of hydraulic-unit drawings and engineering checks of control schematics. Minimum Requirements for Consideration:IMPORTANT: Resumes must include degree program, projected graduation date, and GPA to be considered. We will not be reaching out to obtain information that was requested but not included. Basic Qualifications:Must be currently enrolled in an accredited university and pursuing a degree in one of the following disciplines:At least sophomore status (45 credit hours) completed by May 2027Minimum GPA of 2.75Ability to work 40 hours each week for 12 weeks from May to August. This is a full-time temporary position, so no vacation is accrued. We encourage students to take personal vacations before reporting and between the term ending and their return to school.Must have the ability to travel between multiple facilities and buildings within the industrial complex to support test operations.Must be able to obtain and maintain a security clearance and the AEDC local area networkDue to Air Force Security requirements, U.S. Citizenship is required for employment at AEDCMechanical EngineeringElectrical EngineeringMechatronics EngineeringComputer EngineeringComputer Science or Software Engineering (hard programmers, business systems, data science, Power Platform developers, or machine learning interests; cybersecurity students need to have Security+)Industrial EngineeringAerospace Engineering Preferred QualificationsDemonstrate a positive, self-driven, and adaptable approach; show intellectual curiosity; accept feedback; work effectively with minimal direction.Communicate effectively and demonstrate a willingness to expand technical knowledge and learn new skills.Possess experience with, or familiarity with, PTC Creo, AutoCAD, ANSYS, Excel, MATLAB, and/or 3D-printing equipment and processes.Be able to read, create, and modify mechanical drawings and electrical schematics, including wire tables and cable instrumentation documentation.Show an interest in supporting the nation’s defense; an active security clearance is preferred. Join our Team! U.S. Citizenship is required. jobs.description: Employer: Mead & Hunt, Inc. Expires: 10/09/2026 We are looking for an enthusiastic professional to join our team! At Mead & Hunt, we are employee-owned, value our people, and strive to help everyone succeed. In our transportation group, we're seeking a confident and responsible limited-term transportation engineer intern who can assist with the development of transportation projects across Wisconsin, use design software to prepare engineering and design documents, and develop construction cost estimates for projects. This is an exciting opportunity for a motivated engineering student to gain hands-on experience working on a variety of transportation infrastructure projects in local communities to large interstate projects. In this role, you will work both independently and in teams, solve problems, and learn and apply engineering principles to real-world projects. At Mead & Hunt, our work is guided by core values of taking care of people, doing the right thing, and doing what makes sense. We embrace continuous improvement and encourage creative solutions, always striving to exceed expectations. Respect, teamwork, and personal ownership are at the heart of our culture; we foster collaboration and empower employees to make meaningful contributions. By joining us, you become part of a team that values professional excellence, accountability, and lasting relationships, all while making a positive difference in our communities. What You'll DoAs a Transportation Engineering Intern, you will support transportation engineering projects through a combination of office and field assignments. Responsibilities may include: Work alongside experienced engineers on challenging transportation projectsUse computer assisted programs like Autodesk Civil 3D to prepare engineering and design documents, computations, and quantity estimatesAnalyze and prepare reports, specifications, plans, schedules, studies, permits and other design documents for projectsAssist with CAD-based design work and support the design and plan production of transportation-related projectsSupport roadway, site, and transportation design efforts through calculations, quantity takeoffs, and cost estimatesParticipate in construction inspection, documentation, and field observation activitiesAssist with surveying and data collection effortsPerforming additional duties and special projects as assigned The successful candidate must have:Completed at least two semesters of college-level coursework in Civil Engineering, Environmental Engineering, Construction Management or related field from an accredited college or universityA valid driver's license is required. jobs.description: Employer: ENFOS Inc. Expires: 10/09/2026 ENFOS is redefining how global enterprises manage long-term environmental risk. As the category leader in Environmental Obligation Management, our platform centralizes and automates the full lifecycle of Environmental Remediation Obligations (EROs) and Asset Retirement Obligations (AROs)—replacing fragmented spreadsheets and outdated tools with a purpose-built, multi-tenant SaaS platform.For 25 years, ENFOS has helped the world’s leading industrial companies stay audit-ready, SOX-compliant, and financially in control of their environmental obligations. Privately held and profitable, ENFOS operates with no direct competitors and supports a blue-chip customer base spanning energy and natural resources, chemicals, manufacturing, and logistics end markets.With regulatory pressure rising and ESG scrutiny intensifying, ENFOS is uniquely positioned to empower Finance, Legal, and Remediation teams to improve decision-making, mitigate risk, and drive long-term balance sheet reliability. About the RoleAs a Software Engineering Intern at ENFOS, you will work alongside experienced engineers building and modernizing an enterprise SaaS platform used to manage complex environmental and financial obligations.This is a hands-on engineering internship. You will contribute to real product development and may work across frontend applications, backend services, APIs, data processing, document management, AI-enabled capabilities, or platform infrastructure depending on your technical strengths and current product initiatives.You will participate in the same engineering practices used by our development teams, including design discussions, implementation, code reviews, testing, and iterative delivery, and gain experience building reliable, secure, and scalable enterprise software.We are looking for interns who have strong computer science fundamentals, enjoy solving difficult problems, and are comfortable learning beyond a single technology stack. How We Work: Agile development: Work in two-week sprints with clear goals, ownership, collaboration, and rapid iteration.Engineering quality: Build production-quality software with an emphasis on clean architecture, automated testing, code reviews, security, performance, and long-term maintainability.Modern technology stack: Gain hands-on experience across our technology stack, including Java, Spring Boot, React, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Redis, RabbitMQ, WebSockets, GitLab, Docker, Ansible, and CI/CD, as well as modern AI-assisted development tools.End-to-end engineering: Depending on the project, work across frontend, backend, APIs, data, AI-enabled capabilities, and platform services rather than being limited to a single area of the technology stack.Engineer ownership: Take initiative, solve real problems, and contribute ideas that improve the performance, scalability, reliability, and user experience of the ENFOS platform.Mentorship and growth: Work closely with experienced engineers, participate in technical design and code reviews, and develop the skills needed to build and understand enterprise-scale software systems. ResponsibilitiesAs a Software Engineering Intern at ENFOS, you will work alongside experienced engineers to design, build, test, and improve production software used by global enterprises to manage complex environmental and financial obligations. Depending on your skills, interests, and project needs, you may contribute across frontend, backend, data, AI-enabled features, or platform engineering.You will have opportunities to:Build production experienced engineers. jobs.description: Employer: Giles Flythe Engineers, Inc. Expires: 10/09/2026 2027 SUMMER INTERN - GILES FLYTHE ENGINEERSWANT AN INTERNSHIP WHERE YOU CAN SEE ENGINEERING IN THE REAL WORLD?At Giles Flythe Engineers, our interns aren't stuck behind a desk all summer. You'll be in the field, working alongside engineers, investigating real buildings and structures, solving problems, and seeing your work translate into actual repairs and improvements.Giles Flythe Engineers, Inc. is looking for a Civil, Construction, or Architectural Engineering Intern to join our team this upcoming Summer of 2027 in Raleigh or Charlotte, North Carolina.WHAT YOUR SUMMER WILL LOOK LIKEIn this role, you won't just be learning about engineering in a classroom; you'll have the opportunity to see it in action. You will work alongside engineers to assist property owners in solving problems and understanding building and site improvements through field investigations, technical reports, and repair/construction design.During this internship, you will gain hands-on experience while working on a variety of projects, including:Perform on-site field investigations and structural assessment of existing homes, buildings, or structures.Complete forensic structural engineering evaluations and reports.Work on a variety of HOA and commercial property projects.Effectively and professionally communicate in writing and verbally.Travel to inspection sites, both residential and commercial.WHAT YOU'LL NEED TO BE SUCCESSFUL:Actively pursuing a Bachelor's degree in Civil, Construction, or Architectural Engineering from an accredited engineering program.Prior construction or structural engineering internship experience is desired.Proven technical writing and report writing skills.Strong communication skills with the ability to interact with the team on a daily basis.Ability to work independently but also as part of a team.Ability to work on several projects simultaneously.Willing to perform inspections in crawl spaces, attics, basements and roofs. Must have the ability to bend, stoop, kneel, crawl, climb and balance.Experience using Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Outlook) and AutoCAD a plus.Valid Driver's license with a good driving record.ABOUT GILES FLYTHE ENGINEERS (GFE)Giles Flythe Engineers, Inc. was founded in 2003 with a focus on evaluating buildings and site improvements. We specialize in working with property owners and community associations in problem-solving, repair/maintenance planning, pre-purchase due diligence, cost estimating, and structural design. We work with thousands of properties each year including all types of commercial real estate, high-rise condominium properties, townhome communities and single-family residential properties. Our clients include commercial real estate investors/owners, homeowners, community associations, general contractors and architects.OUR TEAMOur team has a wide range of relevant engineering experience including environmental engineering, structural engineering, site civil engineering, land development, stormwater engineering, mechanical engineering and building envelope evaluations. We have a highly collaborative culture which enables us to readily draw from the experience and expertise of our team. We embrace a decentralized leadership structure relying on empowered autonomous team members to make most decisions.WHY WORK FOR GFE?Giles Flythe Engineers offers a collaborative work environment with competitive salary commensurate with experience, clearly defined bonus plan based on individual performance. We offer health insurance (medical, dental and vision), 401k, paid holidays, paid time off, tuition reimbursement, training and professional development, and gym membership reimbursement. As we continue to grow, we anticipate many future opportunities for career growth and development.Giles Flythe Engineers, Inc. provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws.Applicants must be legally authorized to work for Giles Flythe Engineers in the U.S. without employer sponsorship. We do not typically sponsor H1-B or any other work visa petitions.For more information, or to apply now, you must go to the website below. Please DO NOT email your resume to us as we only accept applications through our website.https://gfengineers.applicantpool.com/jobs/1324496-343413.html

jobs.title: Graduate Systems Engineer at Coherence Protocol
jobs.description: Employer: Coherence Protocol Expires: 10/09/2026 Graduate Systems Engineer — AI InfrastructureM.S. / Ph.D. Students · Part-Time · Coherence Labs AICoherence Labs is building Independent Execution Authority — infrastructure that determines whether an autonomous system’s proposed action is authorized to become real at the moment of execution.As AI moves from generating recommendations to operating software, financial systems, industrial processes, and physical infrastructure, a new systems problem emerges: who decides whether a proposed action may actually commit?We are looking for an exceptional M.S. or Ph.D. student in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field to work directly on that problem.This is not a model-training role. You will work on the runtime infrastructure between an autonomous system’s proposed action and its real-world consequence.What you’ll work onRuntime adjudication and enforcement at execution boundariesDistributed-systems failure semantics and fail-closed behaviorIndependently verifiable authority records and signed execution receiptsEvidence freshness, revocation, supersession, and authority resolutionReplay, deterministic evaluation, and auditabilityAPIs and integration paths for enterprise and industrial systemsPerformance, reliability, concurrency, and adversarial testingProduction architecture as the system moves from evidence-mode deployments toward consequential in-path executionYou will work with the founder and founding engineering team on an existing codebase and architecture. The work is hands-on: reading unfamiliar systems, identifying failure modes, implementing bounded components, writing tests, and defending architectural choices in review.We care much more about how you think than how many frameworks you know.Strong candidates will have experience with some combination of:Distributed systems, operating systems, databases, networking, security, or systems researchPython and/or another systems languageAPIs, services, concurrency, state machines, or transactional systemsCryptographic signatures or authorization systemsTesting failure conditions rather than only happy pathsBuilding substantial research or production software independentlyA Ph.D. is not required. An exceptional M.S. student who has built serious systems is preferable to a Ph.D. candidate whose experience is primarily model experimentation.What makes this unusualYou won’t be optimizing another chatbot or wrapping an LLM API.You’ll be helping define infrastructure for a question that becomes unavoidable as machines gain the ability to act:May this exact action become real, now, on this evidence?Coherence is an early-stage company. The architecture is real, the codebase exists, and the problems are not pre-packaged assignments. You should be comfortable entering an evolving system, figuring out what is actually true, and taking ownership of a bounded piece of it.Location: Remote / Seattle-area welcomeCommitment: Part-time during the academic year; potential for expanded involvementStart: As soon as practicalCompensation: Paid; commensurate with experience and commitmentTo apply, send:Resume/CVGitHub or representative code/researchA short note describing the most technically difficult system you have personally built or debugged — what failed, why it failed, and how you knew

jobs.description: Employer: Steel Dynamics, Inc. - Aluminum Dynamics Expires: 10/10/2026 What Does Steel Dynamics Do?Steel Dynamics is a leading industrial metals solutions company that produces lower-carbon, high-quality steel products primarily from recycled scrap. Interns are not limited to observing from a distance, they actively work alongside operators and maintenance teams on the production floor, applying engineering principles directly to equipment, systems, and processes. This approach allows interns to design solutions, test them in real-world conditions, and see the immediate impact of their work. Internship LocationThis internship is located at the Steel Dynamics Columbus Flat Roll Division located in Columbus, MS. This internship will take place part-time throughout the 2026-2027 school year, with potential to work full-time hours in Summer 2027. Interested students must be located in the Great Columbus, MS area, ideally enrolled at Mississippi State University. What Qualifications Do I Need?RequiredCurrently pursuing a Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Automation/Controls Engineering, or a related field.Basic understanding of programming principles and troubleshooting methodologies.Strong interest in industrial automation, controls engineering, and manufacturing technology.Ability to work effectively in a team-oriented industrial environment.PreferredExposure to programming through coursework, projects, or personal experience.Exposure to electrical, computer, embedded, or control system concepts through coursework or projects.Interest in hands-on troubleshooting and applying engineering concepts in an industrial environment.Previous technical project, laboratory, internship, co-op, or other hands-on experience.Steel Dynamics, Inc., and all affiliated entities are equal opportunity employers.

jobs.description: Employer: Steel Dynamics, Inc. - New Millennium Building Systems Expires: 10/10/2026 What Does Steel Dynamics Do?Steel Dynamics is a leading industrial metals solutions company that produces lower-carbon, high-quality steel products primarily from recycled scrap. Operating through a circular manufacturing model, the company manufactures a wide range of steel products including flat roll, structural, and long products for industries such as construction, automotive, energy, and manufacturing. In addition to steel production, Steel Dynamics operates metals recycling facilities, steel fabrication plants, and aluminum production operations, serving customers across North America with a focus on innovation, efficiency, and sustainability. This is a New Millennium Position. Who is New Millennium?A division of Steel Dynamics Inc. (SDI), New Millennium was founded in 1999 in Butler, Indiana, with one clear mission: To be a trusted collaborator for the design, engineering, and supply of structural steel joists and deck. Today, 25 years later, we’re one of the largest providers of high-performance structural steel joists, joist girders, and deck solutions for commercial steel construction projects. What Makes This Internship Different?The Structural Engineering Internship at Steel Dynamics is unique because interns are not limited to observing or performing routine tasks, they are directly involved in projects that impact production, safety, and long-term infrastructure reliability. Unlike many programs that focus solely on classroom-style assignments, SDI interns gain hands-on experience in both design and field work, from analyzing and drafting structural components to inspecting and reinforcing critical infrastructure in active industrial environments. This combination of office and on-site project involvement provides students with exposure to the full lifecycle of civil engineering work in a manufacturing setting. Many interns also work alongside contractors, operators, and engineers, giving them a broader perspective of how civil engineering integrates with operations and business strategy. The result is an experience that goes beyond traditional internships by preparing students to solve real-world challenges and contribute measurable value from day one. Internship LocationThis internship is located at the New Millennium facility located in Hope, AR, in the Sales Department. This internship will take place during Summer 2027. Internship BenefitsFurnished Housing Free of CostProvided for interns living more than 50 miles from their work site, including essential furnishings to ensure a comfortable stay during the internship.401(k) & Company MatchEligibility to participate in the company 401(k) plan with a 10–50% company match that vests immediately.Employee DiscountsAccess to discounts on hotels, vehicles, and other goods and services through Steel Dynamics’ nationwide partnernetwork.Employee Assistance ProgramUp to five free visits per issue, per year for counseling, legal advice, financial guidance, and other daily living resources.Intern ExtravaganzaA two-day event at company headquarters featuring facility tours, networking with company leaders, cultural immersion, and connecting with other interns from across the country.Competitive PayCompetitive hourly wages for all internship positions, rewarding the value interns bring to the company. What Are My Responsibilities as a Structural Engineering Intern at Steel Dynamics?Apply engineering principles to support ongoing design, analysis, and construction projects ranging from community churches, schools, offices and retail buildings to athletic facilities and fieldhouses to massive warehouses and data centers covering acres of land for the world’s largest distribution and data storage companies.Assist in evaluating and designing structural components such as platforms, open-web steel joists and girders, and welded and bolted connections.Conduct inspections of existing infrastructure to identify potential issues and recommend solutions.Perform experiments, collect field data, and analyze results to guide project decisions and operational improvements.Utilize laboratory and engineering tools, including AutoCAD and BIM software, to create drawings, models, and technical documentation.Collaborate with engineers, contractors, and operations personnel to clarify requirements, coordinate repairs, and support project execution.Ensure compliance with applicable building codes, safety standards, and internal quality expectations.Contribute to day-to-day engineering activities in a fast-paced industrial environment to meet facility needs.Assist sales team with technical knowledge to complete estimates, troubleshoot scope issues with estimating and coordinators to help find issues at bid time.Value engineer to help with design options and partner with key customers to offer competitive options. What Qualifications Do I Need?Candidates should have a strong interest in Structural Engineering, and be enrolled in a Bachelor’s degree program in Civil Engineering or related field, enabling attainment of EIT license and eventual Civil PE licensure.Preferred GPA of at least 2.7Examples of Projects Steel Dynamics Structural Engineering Interns Have CompletedDesign and analyze structures such as buildings, crane runways, mezzanines, platforms, and equipment supports to ensure long-term durability under industrial conditions.Evaluate structural loading, vibration, thermal expansion, and wear to ensure all designs can withstand heavy and dynamic forces over time.Ensure all designs comply with local building codes, OSHA safety regulations, and industry-specific standards through thorough documentation and review.Participate in structural detailing using AutoCAD, converting structural drawings into fabrication-ready drawings and details.Generate finalized modification details to resolve field conflicts and coordinate with information provided by outside parties to ensure project success.Steel Dynamics, Inc., and all affiliated entities are equal opportunity employers.
